slides.texte_overlay:
How to stop feeling awkward at parties
(and actually have fun)
Arrive early. Walking into a room of five people is way easier than walking into a room of fifty. You meet people one at a time, and by the time it fills up, you're already part of the party.

Give yourself a job. Help with the drinks, take the coats, handle the playlist. "Need a hand with that?" Having something to do with your hands kills half the awkwardness and gives you a reason to talk.
Join groups of three, not pairs. Two people talking might be deep in something private. A group of three is open. Stand at the edge, laugh at the joke, and wait for the natural moment to jump in.

Have a few things you're curious about. Five minutes a day on history, art or science gives you real stuff to bring up. "Did you know octopuses have three hearts?" Weird facts beat small talk every time.
slides.texte_sophia: Have a few things you're curious about. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. Weird facts break the ice way better than small talk.

slides.texte_overlay: Ask about the host. "So how do you know Jake?" works on literally everyone in the room. Everybody has a story about how they got there, and it saves you from another round of "So, what do you do?"

Stop replaying what you just said. That slightly weird comment? Everyone forgot it two seconds later. Nobody is analyzing your sentences tonight. You're the only one keeping score, so stop keeping it.
Leave properly. You don't have to be the last one there. Find the host and say "Great night, thanks for having me." A clean goodbye feels way better than slowly fading into a corner until midnight.
